body: Might be worth filing  this on symlink-or-copy, looks like they're missing a try/catch

I'm not sure exactly where the problem is coming from. It shouldn't affect Windows machines, and can be fixed on unix by replacing the `symlinkOrCopySync()` in the tree-stabilizer.ts with `fse.copySync()`, but there are performance implications.

However, I'm not convinced that it's a TreeStabilizer bug. I am expecting this to be multi_copy or the Funnel plugin itself, and possibly just the design of the dart treebuilder, which could be unsafely reusing a tree

issue.title: Maybe don't die on dead symlinks

repository.name: node-symlink-or-copy
repository.description: Symlink files or directories, falling back to copying on Windows

issue.body:
I'm not sure exactly what is causing this problem, it seems to be related to angular's TreeStabilizer plugin implemented to work around the unstable outputPaths issue.

I'm fairly sure the producer of the dead symlinks is one of our own plugins (MultiCopy), but it's very difficult to verify that. Subsequently, symlink-or-copy relies on fs.realpathSync() and throws an ENOENT due to the dead simlink

For some details on how this bug manifests itself, see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/2386

If I had better tools for debugging this, I could do a better job sorting it out, but it is a regression introduced by the implementation of an incremental version of broccoli-merge-trees

body:
Oh, another thing that seems to fix this is re-implementing stew.map (and broccoli-filter) on the new rebuild-api. I guess it's another symptom of broccoli-filter doing crazy things, and the tree-stabilizer not fixing it properly.

Any votes for the approach taken to fix this? It's a one-liner (with negative perf implications) vs several-hundred-lines
